Commentary.Commentary: The second new ball changed things for the touring team on Day 1 as Anderson then came to life. He was well supported by Stokes as the pair hunted down 9 wickets between them. England now would like to bat well and big to take a big lead. The wicket does have something on offer for the pacers but is not a bad one to bat on. The home side has 4 good pacers in their ranks and we can surely expect an interesting passage of play here. Stay tuned.

Windies though did manage to add a few handy runs this morning, they will be disappointed with their overall performance. One can say they have finished with a score slightly under par as they should have had a lot more especially after their top order batted well. 40s from their openers and 50-plus scores from Hetmyer, Chase and Hope saw them well-placed at 240 for 4. Although none went on to make it big and the lower order failed to contribute much. As a result, their first innings' total remained under 300.

The English side is seen walking off with happy faces and they are led off the field by the pacer who bagged a fifer here, James Anderson. A standing ovation for him by the crowd and he deserves every bit of it. Meanwhile, England have asked for a light roller.

OUT! Gone! No hundred for Hetmyer. Caught behind acrobatically by Foakes diving to his left. A fuller length ball on leg and moving away from the lefty, he goes for the full throttle and gives a wild slog. The ball takes the outside edge and it flies to the left of Foakes who takes a lovely catch. Stokes ends with four wickets of his own. WINDIES END ON 289. The last 5 batsmen together have contributed exactly 5 runs from their willows. 3 ducks and the number 11 remained not out on 0. Only Holder got off the mark. An innings that began with a lot of promise ends quite less than what it should have actually gone on to be.
Aimed at the hips once more, flicked away to fine leg by the southpaw but the single is not taken.
Short of a length ball on middle, Hetmyer was lining up for a big shot but decides against it in the end.
Well outside off to end the over, left alone by the no. 11 bat.
Length ball on middle, a front foot defense by Gabriel back towards the bowler.
Shannon Gabriel is the last man to walk in.

OUT! There it is. That is the breakthrough and also the fifth wicket for Anderson. The 27th time he has done in Tests. A typical Jimmy wicket, bowls this one on a good length outside off and makes it tail away very slightly. Too good for the number 10 batsman who pokes at the ball. The ball goes to Buttler at third slip in a good height. He pouches it easily and England after a frustrating 10 overs have finally broken through. The stand worth 25 has ended.
Just short of a good length above middle stump, Alzarri trusts the bounce and lets it go.
Hurls this one on a length down the leg side, left alone by the batsman this time.
Fuller length ball outside off, driven back towards the cover fielder by Joseph.

FOUR! Into the 80s is Hetmyer. However, he would have preferred a single here. This is short again on middle, Hetmyer makes room and then flat-bats it over the bowler's head. Safest area to hit as there is no fielder. A boundary.
A bumper now on middle, Hetmyer evades it.

NOT OUT! Ultra Edge shows nothing there! So not sure what the sound was. Shimron survives to fight another day. Excellent use of the review from him. This is a short delivery outside off. Hetmyer tries to guide it down to third man. There is a noise as the ball passes the bat, an appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger. SH reviews straightaway. Replays roll in and it shows that there was no bat involved.

Hetmyer has been caught behind and it has been given out by the umpire. There was surely some sort of noise on that but the batsman has taken it upstairs for some reason. Maybe he feels he has not touched it. Let's wait for the replays.
Length ball on the middle, pushed to cover.
Peach! Lovely shape from Stokes on this ball. Landed it on middle and got it to swing away and beat the outside edge of Shimron who was trying to defend from the crease.
Outside edge from Hetmyer once more but this time the ball runs all along the ground wide of the slip present. Third man stops the ball but there is no single taken by the batsmen.
As has been the case all morning, Joseph keeps out the last ball of the over well as he defends this length ball on middle from the crease.
Wide outside off, guided towards the third man for a single by Shimron.
Another ball outside off that is left alone by the southpaw.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

Hetmyer is living a charmed life here. Goes for a lofted shot over mid off to this ball outside off on a fuller length. Gets a thick outside edge but the ball goes over first slip. There is a very fine third man who stops the ball. The single is not taken though.
Wide outside off and moving even further away, Shimron chases after the ball looking to cut but can't connect.
Beaten! This is a better ball just outside off and moving away slightly, Joseph plays inside the line and is beaten on the outside.
Very wide outside off, Alzarri goes after the ball but cannot get bat on ball.
Joseph stands in his crease and defends this ball towards short leg.

Brilliant effort from Rory Burns. Hetmyer cuts this one very late and places it wide of third man to his left. The fielder runs and dives before stopping the ball. Saves three there as the batsmen stopped running after one looking at the ball. Poor cricket from the Windies.
Full toss but Hetmyer misses out this time. Mistimes his attempted lofted shot towards mid-wicket. The ball runs towards the bowler.
A fuller length ball outside off, Hetmyer comes ahead and defends the ball onto the ground.
Much better defensive technique this time from Alzarri.

Hit on the pads but the ball was doing too much this time. Height was a factor too on this length ball that landed outside off and came in a long way. Joseph looked to defend the ball but missed it to get hit on his pads.
The batsman has driven it through mid on and they have run through for a single.
Left alone by SH outside off on this occasion.
A front foot defense attempted by Shimron but the ball takes the inside edge and goes onto the pads.

FOUR! Another lucky one for the southpaw. Bowls this outside off, Hetmyer goes for an expansive cover drive. The ball though takes the outside edge and goes over the head of the slip cordon for a boundary. Windies riding their luck here.

Another one with good spice here! Bounces a lot and is aimed at the head of the batsman. Tries to fend it off once more but gets a very faint tickle off the glove that carries over the head of the keeper. Goes behind for a single. Replays show that there was daylight between the bat and ball though, but it was given as runs.

Good bouncer! Aims this short delivery on the rib region, Hetmyer is really uncomfortable and tries to fend it off uncomfortably. The ball takes the gloves but luckily, it does not carry to the keeper behind.
Left alone outside the off stump this time.

FOUR! Brilliant placement from Hetmyer here. A length ball on off stump, Shimron lifts it over the head of an extra cover present but well wide of long off. Runs into the fence after a couple of bounces.
A fuller length delivery on off stump, pushed back towards mid off by SH.
Serves this ball outside off, Hetmyer raises his arms and lets the ball go.
Yorker speared in on the base of off stump, dug out well by Alzarri. Not yet off the mark though.
Swinging fuller length delivery outside off, left alone by Joseph.
Gets to the other end with two balls to go this time. A length ball on off pushed back to long off for a run by Hetmyer.
Another big shot attempted to a very wide ball outside off. Hetmyer connects only with thin air once more. Looks like a set plan from Anderson.
Shimron has played that off the front foot and onto the ground.
Hetmyer chases after this ball wide outside off but misses the ball.
A length ball on middle kept out successfully by Joseph to end the over.
Hetmyer gets to the other end on the fifth ball once more. Guides this length ball outside off towards the deep point region.
Bouncer on middle, SH ducks under it and lets the ball go.
Fuller length ball on middle once more, defended onto the ground by the southpaw on his front foot.
Shimron shoulders arms to let that one through outside off again.
Wide outside off stump, Hetmyer leaves it alone.
Easily defends this full one on middle does Alzarri.
Driven through the covers this time for a single to deep cover. Hetmyer leaves Joseph with one ball to play.

FOUR! Smashed back over the bowler's head! Stand and deliver stuff from the southpaw. A full length ball just outside off, the typical Windies flair comes out as he lofts it right back over the head of the bowler for a boundary.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball back on the off side.
Defended from the crease this time.
The ball is down the leg side but Hetmyer still goes after it but fails to get any bat on it.
A length ball on middle, defended back down the ground by Joseph.
A slower ball yorker that goes as a full toss. Hetmyer failed to read it but manages to adjust well and work it through square leg for a single.
A length ball just on top of off stump, defended back down towards the bowler.
Banged in short outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Pretty full on middle and Shimron times it really well to the left of mid on where Curran makes a good tumbling stop. An easy single would have been available but is not taken.
Delivers this one well outside off does Stokes, left alone by Hetmyer.
Fuller length ball on middle, Alzarri defends it on the front foot.
Left alone outside off by the batsman once more.
Good away swinging delivery outside off, left alone by Joseph.
A push to mid-wicket by Shimron to this one on the pads. The single is taken this time.
A solid defense to this one on a length outside off.
A length ball on middle and slightly coming in, Hetmyer was looking to defend but gets an inside edge that runs to fine leg. The single is not taken.
James Anderson to bowl from the other end.
Yorker but the tail ender manages to keep it out by bringing his bat down just in time.
Another one on a good length, Alzarri stays in his crease and defends the ball.
Joseph comes half ahead and defends this ball onto the ground.
Lots of inswing first up, but the ball was hurled down the leg side. No problem for the no.10 batsman as he lets it go.
The fielders are in position so are the umpires. Alzarri Joseph walks in at number 10 and will take strike against Ben Stokes who has four balls to go in his over.

After a see-saw first day, it is the visitors who head into Day 2 with their noses in front. They now have two wickets to take and they would look to pick it as quickly as possible. The hosts on the other hand, do have Hetmyer out there. One would expect him to come out and look for some quick runs. The hosts would hope he can take them close to the 300-run mark. The wicket did show signs of quickening up toward the end of yesterday. It will be interesting to see how it plays today.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

What can we now expect on Day 2? England continuing their domination or the Windies fighting back? Well, they still have Hetmyer out there and they would hope he could somehow take them close to the 300-run mark. England on the other hand, will want to wrap this up quickly and then bat well. The wicket played well throughout but showed signs of quickening up towards the end. Windies won't mind that though as they have four pacers in their rank. We witnessed an exciting day of cricket today and we can be in store for another tomorrow. Do join us at 1000 local (1400 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

For England, it was hard work for their bowlers today. Anderson was exceptional and was the pick of the bowlers with a four-fer. He was well-supported by Stokes who bowled his heart out and ended with a three-fer. The rest though weren't at their best, not only did they struggle to take wickets but also went for runs. It would have been a different story had they bowled well too.

Windies on the other hand will be disappointed with where they have finished Day 1. They won a good toss and elected to bat, everyone in their top order except for Bravo came to the fore. They seemed like they would get a very good first innings score but they needed someone to score a big one. However, their batters failed to do so, everybody got starts but could not covert and 4 wickets for 24 right at the end suddenly finds the hosts in trouble.

This session - 37.3 overs, 132 runs and 5 wickets. What a turnaround we saw in this last session, actually in the last 10 overs I should say. It was all going smoothly for the hosts when Hetmyer and Chase were going along pretty well but then England decided to take the second new ball and then it was all about them. Anderson took three in no time and then Stokes chipped in with one. Barrage of wickets towards the end sees the day belong to the visitors.

OUT! Stokes strikes now in the last over of the day! A brute of a delivery this one. It is banged in slightly short, takes off after pitching. Roach looks to defend but can't get on top of the bounce. It hits the handle and goes straight into the hands of Root at first slip. His third catch. Roach walks back and with him so do the other players and the umpires as IT IS STUMPS ON DAY 1!
On middle, it is worked towards mid-wicket for a run.
Good length again on middle, it is worked to mid-wicket.
NASTY! Back of a length ball, it keeps on rising after pitching. Roach tries to defend but is hit on the glove due to the extra bounce.
Tucked around the corner for a run.
Back of a length on off, Hetmyer is solid in defense.
On the pads, it is worked to square leg.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
KR tries to play at this one just outsid off but lets it go in the end.
Fuller yorker length ball on off stump, Roach comes ahead and defends with a straight bat.
That one took off from nowhere! Bounces on a length outside off and then rockets off. Foakes collects it over his head.
Another ball outside off and Kemar is content in leaving it.
Wide outside off to the tail ender, Roach lets it go through.
Good one on a length and coming in slightly late, Hetmyer jams it towards backward point for a single.
Kemar Roach walks out to bat at number 9.

OUT! Anderson is on fire here! The Windies batsman are now falling like nine pins. Four-fer for Jimmy and it is his third with the second new ball. He goes full again around off, Holder looks to drive but then checks his shot, maybe because he wasn't to the pitch of the delivery. Ends up chipping it to the right of Anderson who takes a sharp catch in his followthrough. The Windies have completely lost their way here. England now into the tail.
On off, kept out.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Edged but once again it falls short. On a length and around off, Holder looks to defend but due to the away movement. The ball takes the outside edge and goes on the bounce to second slip.
FOUR! Uppish but a boundary. Holder uses his long reach and then drives it square on the off side. A huge gap there and a boundary results.
Excellent! Continues bowling in the corridor of uncertainty. Holder defends it out.
Very full ball outside off, SH drives this but cannot find the gap through the covers.
This time Jason works it away through the square leg region for a single.
Another full length ball on middle, Holder looked to flick that one but missed to get hit high on the pads.
On the pads this time, flicked away wristily for a single to deep mid-wicket.

FOUR! Does not time this one too well but the ball goes wide of the cover fielder and runs away to the fence. The third man fielder cannot come around. It brings up the FIFTY for Hetmyer. His fifth in Test cricket. A great innings so far but he should not throw it away like the guys before him.
Fuller one outside off, Shimron drives it straight to the cover fielder.
No ball! A very high full toss, Hetmyer is surprised by it. The umpire immediately calls it no ball. Stokes is quick to apologize but that will not prevent him from getting a warning.
Jason Holder, the skipper walks in next. Also, Ben Stokes will bowl the next over. Only two overs with the new ball for Curran.

OUT! In the air... gone! Another one bites the dust and once again, England manage to take two in quick succession. The decision of taking the second new ball is proving to be a master stroke here. The leg cutter from Anderson, it is on middle, it takes off after pitching. Dowrich initially thinks of pulling but then seeing the extra bounce, takes his eyes off the ball. It hits the upper part of the bat and lobs towards the slip cordon. Buttler from third slip runs in and takes a dolly. England ending the day on a good note here.
Once again it is on off, Dowrich strokes it to covers.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Goes fuller but does not get the desired movement. It is stroked to mid off.

JAFFA! Banana swing there. Length which starts on middle, it shapes away and beats the outside edge of the bat. Beautiful seam position on that delivery and the curve on the ball was also delightful to watch.
Good length and on middle, it is worked to mid on.

FOUR! Dismissed! A length ball on the off stump line, Hetmyer just punches it back down towards long on. No one moved. The ball reaches the fence. Brilliant batting this. The 250 comes up for the hosts with that shot. 10 runs off that over, an expensive one from Curran.
Wow! What an innovative shot! A fuller length ball on middle and Hetmyer chips it in the air over mid on for a couple of runs. This is how this guy plays.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the backfoot.
FOUR! A creamy cover drive through the gap wide of the cover fielder. Fuller length ball outside off, Shimron comes ahead and a brilliant shot followed.
Very full and driven straight back down the ground towards the bowler.
A short of a length delivery on top of middle stump, Hetmyer defends off the back foot.
On a good length around off, Dowrich gets right behind the line and blocks it.
Shane Dowrich is in at number 7.

OUT! Chase is out of here! Anderson strikes in his second over with the second new ball. He is a class act this guy. The last one came back in sharply, this one goes away and Chase had no answers to it. The length and line is also immaculate. Around off and just behind the driving length. Chase is half forward as he tries to defend. The ball takes the outside edge and goes at a comfortable height to Joe Root at first slip. He takes it with ease. Chase starts walking back but the umpire ask him to wait as they want to check for the no ball. It is just about fine and Chase has to continue his walk back. Another promising stand has been cut short. A good innings from Roston comes to an end. The Windies though would have loved more. Half the side back in the hut for the hosts. Can England pick a couple more before Stumps? 7 overs more to go after this one.
The in-dipper this time, jags back in sharply from middle, Chase tries to flick but misses to get hit high on the thigh pad.
Edged but well short again! Played that with soft hands. Length ball on off, Chase tries to defend but the ball goes off the outside edge and on the bounce to second slip.
Fullish and on off, it shapes away a touch. Chase looks to drive but the ball goes off the inner half back to the bowler.
On the shorter side and outside off, Chase stands tall and punches it through covers for a run.
On the shorter side and on the pads, Chase looks to flick but misses to get hit on the thigh pad. It rolls towards fine leg, the batsmen run a leg bye.
FOUR! Poor bowling and easy pickings for the batsman. Full and on the pads, it did swing back in late but the line was wrong. Chase flicks it to the fine leg fence.
Nicely bowled! He usually gets the ball to tail back in, this time he gets it to leave the batsman from outside off, Chase plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Sweetly timed! Full and on off, Hetmyer strokes it through mid off, Ali gives it a chase and manages to save a run for his side.
On the pads, it is worked around the corner for a run. Brings up Chase's 7th fifty in Tests. A vital knock as he came out when the Windies lost two quickly. He needs to carry on though.
Full and tailing back in, Chase misses the flick and gets hit high on the back pad. An appeal follows but nothing from the umpire.
Sam Curran is back on.
Outside off this time, Hetmyer lets it be. End of the first over with the second new cherry, not a threatening one.
Good length on off, Hetmyer is solid in defense.
Fuller this time and there is a hint of movement away from the batsman. Chase tries to drive but it goes off the inner half towards square leg for a run.
On middle, Chase strokes it to mid on. Not a lot of swing visible in the first three balls bowled with the second new ball.
Back of a length on off, Chase stands tall and punches it to covers.
Good length on off, it is defended.

The second new ball is now available. The English side are seen in a huddle and now it Anderson who comes into the attack. Also, the second new ball has been taken. Not sure what the meeting was about, maybe a discussion whether to take the second new cherry or now.
Another googly on leg stump, Shimron reads it and defends it with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Googly on the pads, Hetmyer sweeps it away fine on the leg side for a couple of runs. Good running that, late in the day.
Goes slower through the air on this one to Hetmyer, the batsman waits patiently and keeps it out.
Short one outside off, cut away to the deep cover-point fielder for a single.
Defended off the front foot by Chase presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted ball on off stump and slight turn on it. Chase waits for the ball and defends it.
This one is slightly slower on off stump, SH pushes it back towards the bowler.
Chase drives this beautifully through the covers but a fielder is present in the deep and only a single can be taken.
Flatter and quicker again on off stump, Shimron punches it towards long off. Straightish cover half-stops it but cannot prevent the single.
Quicker one on the off stump line, Hetmyer comes ahead and dead-bats this.
Flighted outside off, cut away by Roston to deep point for a single.
Hurled in on the pads this time by Root, Chase misses his flick and gets hit on the pads. The ball runs fine for a couple of leg byes. It brings up the 50-run stand between these two.
Tosses this one up, Chase tries to defend this one coming ahead. It takes a thick outside edge and runs wide of slip for a single.
The southpaw has driven it through mid off. One run added to the total.
Flighted ball on middle and leg, Hetmyer defends it onto the leg side with soft hands.
Drifts onto the pads this time, RC works it fine on the leg side for a run.
Flatter one on middle, Roston gets the inside half of the bat as he tried to drive this ball towards mid on.
Flatter one on the off stump, Chase lets the ball come onto his bat as he defends.
Fires it on the stumps, Hetmyer punches it back to the man at covers.
This is eased down to long on for a run.
On the middle pole, Chase drives it back to the bowler.
Quicker and on off, Chase blocks it.
Fuller in length this time, it is stroked to covers.
On off, defended.
Finds the gap through mid on for a single. Chase will face the first ball of the next over.
Driven through the covers by RC.
Flatter ball on middle, defended off the back foot by Chase.

Run-out appeal from the bowler as he gets a fingertip on a very straight drive from the batsman and angles it onto the stumps...It has been taken upstairs. It seemed that Hetmyer had his bat in the crease all along though.

NOT OUT! As we thought so. The ball was flighted on middle, Chase hits it back hard down the ground. Rashid gets a finger tip on it and it hits the stumps at the non-striker's end. Luckily though for Windies, Hetmyer is not backing up and his bat is grounded in the crease. The green signal flashes.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Slower through the air outside off, Hetmyer cuts it away to deep point for a single.
Hurls this pacy and well outside off, Shimron cuts this away to deep point for a single. Quick, quick over that from Root. Looks like he is trying to get to the second new ball really quickly.
Chase works this flatter and quicker ball on the leg side for a single. He gets to the other end.
The southpaw is ahead in defense to this fuller one outside off but the ball goes off the inside edge towards the leg side for a single.
Another quicker one just outside off, SH is on the back foot as he punches it towards cover.
Shimron comes ahead and dead-bats on this occasion.
Fired in on off and middle stump, Hetmyer manages to jam it out towards mid-wicket.
Chase drives this one but does not get the timing he intends. The ball goes to the cover fielder.
Flighted delivery on middle, defended from within the crease by RC.
Well outside off and spinning away from the batsman, he lets it go.
Worked on the leg side towards mid-wicket but no run available.
Flighted one on middle and spinning slightly, Roston is watchful in defense.
Flatter one on middle, Chase rocks back and whips it wide of deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Shortish again outside off, Hetmyer opens the face of the bat and guides it to point.
A little too short this time, Chase goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted ball on off, Chase strokes it back to the bowler. He is getting good drift here.
On the pads, Chase looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
On off, it is kept out.
Just short! Flatter and outside off, Chase looks to punch it through the off side but the ball takes the outside edge. Luckily for the batter it lands just short of Stokes at first slip.

FOUR! It just gets even better now. Short and wide from Rashid, looked like the one that goes the other way. Hetmyer cuts it very late and towards the vacant deep backward point boundary. James Anderson tries to come around from deep cover but cannot reach the ball even with a dive. Big over for the Windies, 16 off it in the end.

SIX! That is huge! That's how this guy bats. A flighted ball outside off, Hetmyer comes ahead a bit and lifts it over the long off boundary and deep into the stands. A strike rate of more than 100 for him now.
Oooh! A slight outside edge from Chase this time but the ball runs all along the ground towards short third man for a single. It brings up the 200 for the hosts.
FOUR! Finds the gap through the covers this time. Lots of flight on this one and Chase drives it wide to the left of mid off for a good boundary.
Defended off the front foot by RC presenting the full face of the bat.
A flatter one outside off, Hetmyer nudges it towards deep cover for a single.
Adil Rashid to replace James Anderson from the Joel Garner End. The helmet comes off for Shimron Hetmyer.
Slightly shorter length now, worked away to deep mid-wicket for a single. Shimron keeps strike.
Around the wicket to the lefty, fires it in on off stump. Hetmyer comes ahead and defends it onto the ground.
Flatter one on the pads, worked away to deep square leg for a single by the right-hander.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Arm ball on middle, pushed back down the ground by the batsman.
Flatter one outside off, slight drift on it. Chase comes ahead and defends it.
Joe Root, the skipper decides to come on for a bowl now.
A tad more outside off, Roston manages to push it in the gap towards deep point for a single. Retains the strike.
Length ball outside off, defended with a straight bat by Chase.
Coming in with the angle from around the wicket, Shimron drops it towards mid-wicket with soft hands and a quick single is taken.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! Smashed! Overpitched outside off and Hetmyer takes a stride ahead and creams his drive through the covers for a boundary. Buttler won't be liking this at all.
A short of a length ball on the off stump line, Hetmyer gets a thick outside edge that runs towards the gully fielder.

Drinks break. Half of the lengthy third session has been played. England will be delighted to have gotten Shai Hope's wicket but will like a few more in the remaining overs. Meanwhile, Windies would like Chase to remain solid and Hetmyer to make the most of the life given to him. Let us wait and watch what happens in the final passage of play today...
Now strokes this down to long on and takes a run. Smart batting.

SIX! Jos Buttler won't enjoy watching this but we surely enjoyed this shot. Hetmyer uses his feet for the third time in a row, this time gets to the pitch of it and lofts it over the long on fence. This is how he plays, he stays for longer, we are in for some entertainment.
Dances down the track again but does not get to the pitch of the ball this time, it is pushed back towards the bowler.
Daces down the track but ends up yorking himself. It is jammed out.
Flatter and on middle, Hetmyer keeps it out off the back foot.
On middle, Hetmyer defends it out.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump. End of what could have been another successful over.
Back of a length on off, Chase blocks it out.

DROPPED! Easy chance that! Windies could have, actually should have been five down. Buttler is the culprit. It is just ahead of a length outside off, Hetmyer tries to drive it on the up, he does so uppishly towards short cover. Buttler there dives to his right and gets two hands to it but fails to hang on. Hetmyer would like to make this reprieve count. The batsmen take a run.
Angles this one into the batsman, it is a little too straight though. Worked to mid-wicket.
Goes back to bowling on off, Hetmyer goes back and keeps it out.
Trying to swing it from leg stump to the off but there is no movement, it is flicked through mid-wicket for a couple.
Flatter delivery outside off, Chase goes back in his crease and punches it but the ball goes straight towards the cover fielder.
Chase comes ahead to this flighted ball on middle and defends it onto the ground.
Hetmyer gets off the mark as he works this flatter ball on the pads towards mid-wicket and runs to the other end.
Shortens the length this time, worked on the leg side by Chase towards deep square leg for a single.
Another excellent diving stop from Anderson towards his left at cover. Prevents what would have been a certain boundary. This could frustrate the batsman.
Flatter one bowled outside off, Chase drives it all along the ground towards a deepish mid off. No run as the ball was timed too well.
Good length on off, Hetmyer this time gets bat to ball and defends it onto the ground.

Lovely stuff here! Anderson now seems to have his tail up here. He angles it into the batsman from around the wicket and then gets it to leave him. Hetmyer tries to defend but is done in by the away movement. The ball whizzes past the outside edge. Not a lot you can do with that, just hope it does not take the edge.
Back of a length on off, Hetmyer defends it by standing tall.
Good length on off, Hetmyer is solid in defense.
Shimron Hetmyer is out to the middle at number 6.

OUT! Anderson gets Windies' talisman. From 126 for 1, Windies are now 174 for 4. Hope fails to convert and he trudges off slowly, disgusted with himself is the no. 3 batsman. He probably takes along with him the hopes of the Windies getting to a big first innings score. Anderson on the other hand is a delighted man. He is finally rewarded for continuously bowling in the avenue of apprehension. It is once again bowled there, this one comes back in a little. Hope looks to punch it away from his body but does not account for the movement. He ends up playing it outside the line. The ball takes the inside edge and goes into the mitts of the keeper.
Length delivery and outside off, Hope shoulders arms to it.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Another run as Hope this time flicks it through mid-wicket. Looking at ease against Moeen who is getting no purchase from the wicket.
An easy run this time as it is flicked through mid-wicket.
Flatter again on middle, Chase pushes it towards mid on. Short mid-wicket runs to his left and saves a run.
Flatter and outside off, Chase pushes it to covers.
Tosses it up on off, Chase lunges and keeps it out.
Back of a length again on off, Hope once again defends it to point.
Solid off the front foot and now solid off the back foot as he guides this to the man at point.
Fullish and on off, it is eased to mid off. Hope is really hitting the ball off the middle.
On a length and around off, it is guided to point.
Slightly fuller and it comes back in. Hope times it right off the middle but finds mid off.
Outside off, left alone.

SIX! All the way! Top shot! Stand and deliver! Moeen tosses it up around off, Chase clears the front leg and lofts it over the long on fence. He hit that with the spin so the risk factor was not a lot.
Lands it on off again and Chase keeps it out.
Lands it outside off from around the wicket, it is pushed to mid off.
The batsman has played the square drive. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On the shorter side, Hope goes back and pulls it to mid on.
A little too full again, Chase strokes it towards mid on. Root there runs to his left, dives and keeps it down to one.
Another length delivery and on off, Hope defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Streaky but effective. On the shorter side, Hope stands tall and tries to guide it through the gully region, he gets an outside edge which races to the third man fence.
Full and on middle, it is stroked nicely but straight back to the bowler.
Another delivery outside off, left alone.
The away swinger this time but the line is a little too wide outside off, left alone.
Starts off right on the money. On a length and around off, this one jags back in. Hope tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
James Anderson is back on.

Ends the over with a lovely delivery. This is flighted and it is landed just behind the driving length. Chase goes for the drive through the off side but gets beaten. An appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head. There was a noise but it was of the bat hitting the ground.
Quicker and outside off, it turned back in. Chase blocks it out off the back foot.
Better! Flatter and behind a driving length, it skids through. Chase tries to defend but the ball takes the outside edge and goes on the bounce to Stokes at first slip.
Slightly overpitched again, this is closer to the off pole and hence, Chase times it to mid off.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Easy this. A full toss this time on off, Chase once again strokes it through covers to fetch himself another boundary.

FOUR! Welcome back into the attack, Moeen. This is tossed up very full outside off, the spin is out of contention, hence easy pickings for the batter. He reaches out for it and strokes it through covers. The ball races away.
Moeen Ali replaces Ben Stokes who seemed to have tired after bowling for a long time.
Fuller one to end the over, Hope clips this one towards the straighter of the two mid-wickets present.
Served on a good length outside off, Hope defends it with soft hands.
A pushy cover drive but the ball goes straight to the fielder.

Too full outside off, Chase comes ahead a step and bends his knee as he drives this beautifully through cover point. The timing is not excellent and it allows Bairstow to chase the ball and stop it just inside the rope. Three runs are taken. The 150 comes up for the hosts.
Gets this one to come in with the angle as well as the breeze, Roston works it towards mid-wicket.
Around the wicket now, Chase has no hassles defending this ball that is on a length just outside off.
A fuller length ball outside off that is driven straight back towards mid off by Hope.
Effort ball from Stokes. Bouncer on middle and leg but Shai is happy to duck under it and let the ball go.
A ball served outside off on a short length, Chase rocks back and cuts it through point for a single. Moves into double figures with that one.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
A short of a length ball that is bouncing a bit more than Chase expected it to. The ball also comes in and cramps the batsman for room as he tried to guide it in the gap between slip and gully.
A length ball outside off, Chase pushes it back towards the bowler.

Short of a length outside off, Hope stands tall and punches it behind point for a couple of runs. It brings up his FIFTY! His fifth in Test cricket. Great innings so far but needs to carry on and go on to make a big one here.
Curran strays on to the pads and gets flicked for a single down to fine leg.
FOUR! Too full on this occasion and Chase is quick to prowl on it. Goes for the expansive cover drive and gets it to the fence as he finds the gap wide of mid off.
Another one that is just dead-batted by RC.
Moeen Ali was seen warming up after the previous ball.
A good solid back foot defense by Chase to this one on a short length.
Curran delivers this one on a length outside off, Hope guides it towards third man for a single.
Bowls this one very full and way outside off stump, it is an easy leave for RC.
Chase fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad. A strong appeal from the bowler and fielders. The umpire shakes his head and with good reason too. It was a tad too high.
Another short length ball that is defended off the back foot by Chase.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the backfoot.

Surely saved three there! A full length ball outside off, Hope drives hard but a diving Anderson at cover gets his hand to the ball and half-stops it. Only a single is taken. It would have been a sure boundary. Brilliant effort. Lifts the whole team.
Short of a length delivery above middle stump, Hope is on his toes as he defends this one.
Chase tries flicking a ball that is down the leg side but fails to get bat on it. Maiden over.
Short of a length ball outside off here, a back foot punch follows but the ball runs straight to point.
A solid push from the batsman towards the covers.
Gets this one on the off stump line, RC manages to keep it out towards the leg side bringing his bat down in time.
Left alone by Roston as this one is served well outside off.
Short of a length ball outside off, Chase stands tall and punches it towards cover.
Under edge! A bouncer outside off, Hope looks to cut it away but the ball does not bounce as much as the batsman expects it to. Takes the under edge and rolls to the slip cordon.
Tries to tuck up Chase by bowling it on his hips, the batsman manages to work it fine on the leg side for a run to fine leg.
Played back down the ground confidently but not with much timing this time off a length ball on off and middle.
Goes wide of the crease to create an angle, Chase is solid in defense though.
Bowls this one on the off stump line, Roston defends it back standing tall.
Another length ball on the pads, Chase misses his flick and gets hit on the thigh pad. The ball runs fine but there is no chance for a leg bye.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! A very short length ball and it sits up to be hit. Hope gleefully accepts the bad ball and pulls it away for an easy boundary. No pace for Curran to trouble the batsman with a short ball.
A back foot push towards point for no run from Shai.
Fuller length ball and this carries on with the angle outside off. Left alone by SH.
Shape again after landing on middle, Shai works it to mid-wicket.

A very full length ball on middle and shaping in slightly. Hope drives it back down the ground but Curran gets low to his right and stops the ball. Also, flicks the ball back onto the stumps at the non-striker's end. Chase never went out of the crease though.
A good length ball on middle, a straight bat is presented in defense by Roston.
Length ball outside off, Shai guides it with soft hands wide of point. Waits a little before confirming that the ball is away from the fielder and then runs through to the other end.
A good solid defense from Hope to a shorter length ball outside off.
It seems to be a plan this, bowls this one on the hips once more. There is a leg gully in place. Chase manages to guide it fine though for a single.
Length ball going down leg, Roston fails to get any bat on that one.
Bouncer to start off! Chase ducks under that one and lets it go through.
Ben Stokes to continue bowling from the other end.
A length ball on top of off stump, Hope defends it with soft hands.

We are back! Good news! The weather has cleared and the players are back out in the middle. The England team is in a huddle and all set to go for the final session. It will be an extended one. What's in store? Let's find out...Curran to bowl the one remaining ball in the over to Shai Hope.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

EARLY TEA has been taken due to the rain stoppage. This session has gone to the visitors and more so, Ben Stokes in particular. He removed the well-set Brathwaite first and then got rid of Darren Bravo who returned to whites after a very long time. Shai Hope is looking solid in the middle but will need partners to ensure Windies don't throw away the good work done in the morning session. Hopefully the rain will clear away quickly and we resume post the time allotted for Tea.
1414 Local - Now then! This wasn't expected but the heavens have opened up. The covers are brought on. Doesn't look it is going to be a long delay though.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump again.
Shai shoulders arms to this one which is going well outside off.
A length ball outside off, going on with the angle. Hope defends it late towards the slip cordon.
Shortens the length this time outside off, left alone once more.
Bowls this one on a length outside off, Hope decides not to go after that one.
Sam Curran is back into the attack now. Had bowled 5 overs at the start of the day.
This is really good bowling from Stokes. Full effort once more and he goes for a yorker on middle. Hope manages to jam it out towards fine leg for a single. He will keep strike.
Very full this time outside off, Chase reaches out and plays it wide of point for a single.
Short of a length  ball on middle, the batsman plays the bounce and defends it back down the ground.
Outside off and not a great shot from Chase as he chases this one wide away from his body. Gets an inside edge that goes towards short leg.
Bouncer! Roston ducks under it and lets it through to Foakes.
Length ball on top of off stump, Chase defends on the off side and looks for a single but is sent back wisely by his partner.
On off, kept out.
On the stumps, it has been defended.
Flatter and on off, Hope guides it to point.
Flatter and on middle, the batter goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
This is tossed up on off, Chase strokes it back to the bowler.
Flatter and on off, it is pushed to cover-point for a run.
Length ball outside off, Roston is half-ahead in defense.
Short of a length once more, Chase defends it really late towards the slip cordon.
Short of a length ball, defended back down the ground off the back foot.
Wide outside off to the new batsman and shaping away, no need to play at those.
Roston Chase walks in next.

OUT! One brings two! That is exactly the case here for Stokes. What a top delivery this is. It has been pace, pace, pace all this while. This time though he rolls his fingers across the delivery and the length is extremely full, a yorker almost. Bravo is foxed completely. He plays down the wrong line, the ball hits him on the pads. An appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger. Bravo walks back without even thinking of reviewing it as he knew he was a dead duck. He does not trouble the scorers a lot and a poor return to the team for him.
Loose stroke that, just not needed especially so early in the innings. It is a full ball outside off, Bravo who is facing his fourth ball, goes after it but gets beaten.
Shorter length this time, punched back to the bowler by the batsman. Good over from Adil.
Another flatter one outside off, Hope plays for the spin and gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Quicker and straighter on middle, defended back towards the bowler.
Flighted outside off, driven to cover for no run by Hope.
Hurled on middle and slightly turning in, Bravo tucks it fine on the leg side for a single.
Flatter one on middle, Bravo defends with soft hands.
Fullish and on middle, Hope strokes it to mid on. End of a successful over by Stokes.
A bumper to welcome the new batsman, Bravo works it uppishly but away from the square leg fielder for a run.
Darren Bravo walks in at number 4, replacing Kraigg Brathwaite.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Stokes provides the breakthrough England needed so desperately. End of the 73-run stand and Brathwaite's gritty knock has been cut short. A well-deserved wicket this for Stokes, he has looked threatening throughout and finally gets one. Alters his length this time, he has been slightly short but bowls it just ahead of a length he was bowling. It is around off, pitches and straightens just a touch. Kraigg ends up defending inside the line. The ball takes the outside edge and goes into the hands of first slip. Root makes no mistake. Stokes is ecstatic. England would hope this opens the floodgates.
On off, Brathwaite shuffles across and defends it onto the ground.
On the leg side, it is worked around the corner for a single.
A bumper but it is down the leg side, ducked under.

A very fast moving hour of play. 16 overs have been bowled. The two Windies batsmen have carried on superbly after Lunch, looking really solid. Will there be a mistake from them? Or can the English weave some magic against the run of play? They will have to or else it could be a really long day out in the sun.
Very slow but short, it pitches and then turns away. Kraigg goes back and keeps it out.
This time it is on the stumps but KB is solid in defense.
Flatter and outside off, it is the flipper, the batter makes a leave.
The batsman has driven it through mid off.
Tosses it above the eye line and lands it on middle, Brathwaite works it against the turn to mid on. Hope thinks about a single but is rightly sent back by his partner.
Slower through the air on off, it pitches and then turns away. Hope pushes it through covers and gets to the other end.
Back of a length to Brathwaite this time, he easily defends it.
That in between length by Stokes around off, Hope is not sure whether to come forward or stay back. He has a tentative push at it, the ball goes off the outer half through point for a run.
A little fuller on middle, Hope strokes it to mid on. Seems a lot more comfortable with the deliveries pitched up.

Almost drags it on! Three very good balls by Stokes here. This is also on a back of a length on off, it pitches, angles in and also skids through. Hope tries to defend away from the body but the ball hits the inside edge and goes towards the keeper.
This time he angles it into the batter, Hope works it with that angle to mid on.

Top delivery! Stoke now first angles it into the batter due to which Hope has to play at it. He tries to with a back foot defense. The ball though pitches and then moves away, beats the outside edge by a whisker.
Kraigg though now goes three ahead of him as he works this one fine on the leg side and collects a brace.
On the shorter side, Hope hits it towards sweeper cover and gets to the other end. He is now one run behind Brathwaite.
On the stumps this time, it is blocked.
The googly, Brathwaite waits for the ball to do its bit and then guides it through the off side for a single.
Flighted ball on off, Hope at the very end opens the face of the bat and guides it through cover-point for a single.
Short ball and Hope slaps it hard but straight to the man at covers.
On the fuller side but the line is outside off, left alone.
Driven towards the mid on region.
Back of a length again on off, Kraigg is solid in defense.
On a good length and around off, Kraigg defends it onto the ground.
On the shorter side this time and the line is once again outside off, Hope stands tall and slaps it through covers for a run.
A little movement away from the right-hander after landing it around off, Hope shoulders arms to it.
Ben Stokes has been called on to bowl, replacing James Anderson. He was bowling from the other end in the previous session.
Gives it a little more air outside off, enticing the batsman for a drive. Kraigg though has shown excellent patience till now and he continues to do so as he makes another leave.
Ben Stokes seen warming up.
Extra bounce this time as the ball lands on middle, KB though goes back and does well to defend it onto the ground.
On middle, Kraigg prods forward and keeps it out.
Tosses it up on off, Brathwaite lunges and keeps it out.
Flatter and outside off, Hope slaps it through covers and another run results.
On the shorter side around off, Brathwaite goes back and cuts it through point for a single.
Now makes a leave as the ball is outside off. 8 runs from the over.

FOUR! This is even better than the last one! Class! Not a bad delivery, it was slightly full and on off, Hope leans into it and strokes it through extra cover, it races away. That was a textbook cover drive.
Back of a length on off, Hope goes back and defends it onto the ground.
FOUR! That went to the boundary in a jiffy! Short and outside off, Hope stylishly cuts it through point and the ball races away. First boundary after Lunch.
Pulls his length back but the line is outside off, Hope lets it be. The ball goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Very full and on off, it is stroked to the man at mid off.
A dot ball to end the over. The Windies seem to be at ease here.
Another one outside off, Kraigg comes well ahead and plays it with soft hands.
On the pads once more, Shai flicks it away towards deep square leg. Bairstow comes in quickly and prevents the second run.
Hope defends this one on middle from within the crease.
This one is flatter and hurled down the leg side, KB misses his flick and the ball runs fine for a leg bye after hitting the thigh pad.
Pushed through quicker outside off, Brathwaite comes ahead and defends it towards cover.
Short and wide, Hope misses out! He goes for the cut but mistimes it and the ball goes straight towards the cover fielder. Was a real good chance to get a boundary.
A slightly shorter length ball on middle, SH defends from within the crease.
Gets this one to come in a bit after landing but Hope has no issues as he defends this ball back to Anderson.
Left alone this time as the ball was wide outside off and swinging away.
Short of a length delivery, Shai rides the bounce and defends it onto the ground.
A length ball on middle, Hope slightly moves forwards and plays this one with a straight bat.
The batsman defends the ball from the middle of his bat. An erratic over from Rashid considering the lengths.
Shai goes back in his crease and punches the ball towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Hope prods ahead and pushes this one to the cover fielder.
Short once more, enough time for Brathwaite to rock back and cuts it away to deep cover for a single.
Full and flighted outside off, pushed to cover by Kraigg.
Very short this time, Hope rocks back deep in his crease and pulls this away to deep mid-wicket for a single. The 50-run stand comes up.
Goes fuller this time but the ball is outside off, Brathwaite is in no mood of going after those.
Stump-to-stump line again, Brathwaite has no problem in defending it out.
On off, blocked.
On the pads, the batter tries to flick but misses, it hits his pads and rolls towards the fine leg region. A leg bye taken.
Full and outside off, the batter makes a leave.
A little bit of shape away from off, Hope blocks it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Brathwaite comes ahead and dead-bats the final ball of the over.
Another ball on the pads, flicked away to the deep mid-wicket for a single.
Once again cut away to the deep cover fielder for a single. The 100 comes up for the visitors. They would have surely taken this at the Toss.
Pushes this one quicker outside off, cut away to deep point for a single by Hope.

Was that a chance? No it wasn't. The ball was on the pads and Hope flicked it away but found the short leg fielder's leg. Saved at least a couple there did Jennings. Was disappointed for some reason, maybe considering how good he has been at that position in his career so far.
Flatter one outside off, Hope rocks back and punches it to mid off.

Good ball just outside off to end the over, no issues for the batsman though as he defends it solidly from the middle of the bat. Only 9 runs off the first 5 overs after Lunch, good tight stuff from England here.
Delivers this one wide outside off, Brathwaite wants nothing to do with it.
On a good length just outside off, Kraigg presents a straight bat in defense.
Well outside off and shouldered arms to, once more.
Length ball outside off and angling away, left alone by KB.
Length ball outside off and some shape on it, Brathwaite defends it with soft hands on the off side.
Another single to end the over as Kraigg works it towards the mid-wicket region for a single. Retains strike.
Direct hit! No issue though as Hope was well in. Pushed this one towards mid off and was off for a quick single. Good running by the batsmen.
A googly this time and the batsman picks it up as he drops it with soft hands towards mid-wicket and runs through for a quick one.
Brathwaite prods ahead and dead-bats this ball on middle.
Flatter one on leg stump and turning a bit, Hope works it away wristily to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Short and wide outside off, cut away to deep cover-point for a single by Brathwaite.
Outside off yet again, yet again no shot offered.
Hurls this well outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Length ball on the middle and leg stump line, defended back down the ground with a straight bat.
Left alone by Shai once more as it is outside off.
Swinging away after landing outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Fuller length ball on middle, Hope on-drives this but it goes straight to the fielder at mid on.
Shortens the length on the pads, flicked away to the square leg region for a single by Shai.
Finally manages to find the gap as Hope gets his drive wide of the cover fielder. A couple is taken by the time the fielder in the deep covers up. Good running!
Pushed by the batsman towards the cover fielder once more.
Drives this on a bounce to the fielder at cover.
Good ball that outside off, no problems for Hope though as he comes ahead and defends it.
Pretty flat and full outside off, driven just wide of mid off by Hope but he decides against the single.
Adil Rashid to bowl from the other end.
On the hips and worked away fine for a single by Hope. He keeps strike.
Some outswing on this occasion, left alone outside off by the batsman.
A good length delivery on off stump line, Hope stands tall and defends this onto the ground.
Very full and outside off, Shai drives it but does not get good timing on it.
Length ball on the pads, pushed to mid-wicket.
A length ball outside off to start with, Hope keeps it down towards the gully fielder.
Welcome back for the second session of play. Can the hosts continue the good work? We will find out now as the players take their positions. Shai Hope to take strike to James Anderson.
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

The visitors on the other hand, did not look at their best. There was swing on offer earlier for their bowlers but they could not capitalize. Moeen Ali is the sole wicket-taker but has not looked that threatening since. England will hope for a few quick wickets after the break. Do join us to find out who dominates Session 2.

An excellent session for the Windies, everything right from the toss has gone their way till now. They elected to bat and their openers gave them the ideal start adding 53. It was the debutant, Campbell who did majority of the scoring but missed out on a well-deserved half ton. Hope then carried on the good work and he with Brathwaite who is started to get into his own now are amidst a good stand. Windies would hope the two can continue and build a big stand.
A pushy-drive from Brathwaite towards cover brings the over to an end. A maiden. It also is LUNCH ON DAY 1! 30 overs bowled in the session, excellent over rate from the visitors.
The batsman covers the spin on the ball and defends it.
Flatter one on middle, Kraigg rocks back and works it to mid-wicket.
Driven to mid off this time.
Another front foot defense from KB.
Flatter one outside off, Brathwaite comes ahead and defends it onto the ground.
Should be the last over before Lunch...
Another very full delivery on middle, once again it is played with the turn to mid on.
Very full on middle, it is hit down to mid on.
Flatter and outside off, Brathwaite guides it through point and takes a single.
Eased through covers and the batter takes a single.
Flatter and outside off, it is kept out.

Almost! Ali bowls it slightly quicker and fuller. Brathwaite instead of coming forward tries to play it from his crease. He gets his bat down at the very end, it hits the inner half and goes towards fine leg for a run.
Hope keeps the last ball out. 4 runs off Rashid's first over.
Brathwaite comes ahead a bit this time and flicks it away to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Another single to deep cover this time, off the bat of Shai Hope.
Flicked away wide of mid on by Brathwaite for a single to this full ball on middle.
Another flighted one, KB waits a long time and lets the ball come onto the bat.
Lots of air on this one bowled on leg, flicked away to deep mid-wicket by Hope for a single.
Adil Rashid, the leggie is now into the attack.
Brathwaite pushes this wide of mid off but no run is available.
Another flatter one on middle, kept out towards short leg with soft hands.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter one outside off, punched to deep cover for a single by Hope.
Lots of air outside off, driven hard towards cover by Hope.
Flatter one on middle, pushed to deep mid-wicket for a single by Brathwaite.
Another leave outside off from Hope to end the over.
Hurls this way outside off, left alone.
Bouncer! Shai ducks under it and lets it go through.
Shortens the length and SH goes back in his crease to defend it.
FOUR! That is the second time Hope has driven Stokes back down the ground for four. Balance and timing, that was what it was all about. Lovely on the eye.
A length ball outside off, Hope drives this slightly uppishly but straight towards cover.
Pushed back to the bowler off the front foot to end the over. Moeen has picked up the only wicket to fall so far but has been considerably expensive as well.
Flatter one on middle, defended towards short leg by KB.
Flatter one outside off, cut away to deep cover for a single.
Rapped on the pads but it is too high once more! A flatter one outside off and good turn on it as it beats Hope and raps him high on the pads.
Short outside off this time, a mistimed cut from Kraigg results in a single to deep point.
Flighted outside off, Brathwaite drives it back down the ground.
Kept out comfortably this time by SH off a good length.
Fuller one outside off, Hope fails to time his drive as he can only push it towards mid off.
Moves this one the other way and Shai is beaten as he tries to stand tall and cut it away.

Too high! Stokes is getting the ball to swing in but there is good bounce on the wicket. This one lands on a length outside off and beats Hope and raps him on the pads. But it would have gone over the wickets.
Fuller length ball on the pads, worked towards mid-wicket.
A good length ball straightening after landing on off, Hope defends from the crease.
Left alone very late outside off this time by Kraigg.
A touch slower this time, Brathwaite comes ahead and then defends the ball.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
KB comes ahead and dead-bats this one.
FOUR! Beautifully flighted and Brathwaite takes the invitation as he has his dancing shoes on. Lifts this wide of mid on and into the fence.
Flatter ball on a length outside off, Kraigg defends with soft hands towards short leg.
Another short of a length ball going down leg and SH ducks third time this over.
Bouncer once more and Shai ducks under it once more.
A length ball coming in from outside off, defended back towards the bowler off the back foot.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Another good drive but it goes straight to cover this time.

FOUR! Elegant and beautiful! A fuller one outside off and Hope stands tall and off drives this right back down the ground wide of mid off. No stopping those, just go pick the ball from outside the fence.
Very well defended this time as a follow up to the huge one. Good over for the Windies, 12 off it in the end.

SIX! Bratwaite seems to have seen enough now. Comes down the track and lofts this over deep mid-wicket. The ball lands just outside the rope. The first maximum of the game. Moves into the 20s does Kraigg.
Defended by the batsman coming ahead.
Another quick single, would have been really tight had mid on hit this time. Uneccessary that, from Windies. Looked like Hope was desperate to get off the mark and hence ran.
A flatter one on middle, KB pushes this towards mid on and picks up a quick single.
FOUR! Full and flighted outside off, Brathwaite comes ahead and drives this hard through the vacant cover region. No fielder back there and it runs to the fence.
Back of a length outside off, Shai lets it be.
Another in-dipper but this is on the pads, Hope fails to flick as he is hit on the pads.
That swing back in a long way! Full and way outside off, it tails back in a lot. Hope first thinks of driving it but then pulls out of the shot.
On the shorter side, Brathwaite hops and taps it towards point for a quick run.
A little more fuller on off, Brathwaite defends it out.
Back of a length on off, Kraigg defends it onto the ground.
Prods forward this time and works it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Slower through the air outside off, Hope maybe should have played this delivery off the front foot, he though goes back and defends it onto the ground.
Flighted delivery on off, Hope pushes it to covers.
On the stumps this time, it is defended onto the ground.
Tosses it up outside off, Hope covers his off stump and makes a leave.
Shai Hope walks in at number 3.

OUT! Plumb in front! The debutant goes 6 shy of a fifty. He was going for his shots and eventually that brings about his downfall as he went for one too many. A full and flighted ball on middle, Campbell goes for the sweep but misses it and gets rapped bang in front of middle. The umpire has no hesitation and raises his finger immediately. The debutant started walking away immediately and with good reason too. It would have been a waste of a review had it been taken as replays show us that it would have hit middle of middle stump. The first one down for the Windies and spin was the reason.

FOUR! 50 up! Ideal start by the openers. A boundary to bring up the 50-run stand. It is not off the middle though. No gully however so it races to the fence. Full and wide outside off, Brathwaite goes after it, he gets an outside edge and the ball crosses the third man fence.
On the shorter side again, Campbell once again it hurried into the pull shot, he mistimes it towards square leg for a run.
On a good length around off, it is kept out.
Outside off, it is left alone.

On the shorter side and on the body, even before Campbell swivels to pull, the ball hits him on the thigh pad and rolls towards fine leg. A leg bye taken. However, the umpire has signaled it as a dead ball as he feels the batsman did not offer a shot.
FOUR! Oozing in confidence is the debutant! That has been creamed! Into the 40s is John. Full and outside off, Campbell strokes it through covers and you need not run for those.
Tosses it up on off, Brathwaite covers the stumps and blocks it. 9 from Ali's first, an expensive start by him.
Flatter and on middle, it is flicked towards mid-wicket with the turn.
No sweep shot this time, he lunges and works it towards mid-wicket for a run.

Top edge but safe! John once again goes for the sweep but this time Moeen slows it up and also bowls it outside off, gets it to bounce extra. The ball hits the top edge and lands in no man's land in the square leg region. Two taken.
FOUR! Swept and swept fine! Campbell this time hits it right off the middle and it races to the square leg fence.
Brings out the paddle sweep, he is helped as Moeen fails to land the ball. The batter picks up two as the ball is fielded at fine leg.
First sight of a spinner this morning. Moeen Ali has been called on to bowl.
This one is the in-dipper on off, KB takes a hand off his bat and works it to square leg. Stokes is really getting the ball to bounce here.
Sprays this one down the leg side, it is left alone.
Angles this one into the pads, looking to get Braithwaite LBW. He though gets his bat down in time and works it to mid-wicket.
Good delivery! The effort delivery this one, bends his back and lands it around off, Kraigg looks to defend but is done in by the extra bounce. The ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Changes the length and bangs it short, Brathwaite ducks under it.

Full and outside off, Campbell looks to drive but gets an inside edge down to fine leg and a single is taken. Not sure if unintentionally or deliberately, Campbell is a touch late on his shots against Stokes.

Drinks break. A solid hour for the hosts, they have done well to not lose a wicket. There have been a few plays and misses but the important fact is no breakthroughs for the English. The debutant has looked good as well. Expect spin to come on soon.
This is comfortably left alone by the batsman as the first hour of play comes to a close.
Beaten! A beauty from Anderson! Length ball on off, looks like it was coming in but it swings away very late and beats the outside edge of Brathwaite.
A straight one on off stump and on a good length, pushed back on the front foot.
Another Brathwaite leave as this one outside off swings away late.
Left alone outside off this time.
Bowls this full and on the legs, defended back down the ground after coming across by Brathwaite.
Changes the angle and lands it on off, he slants it away. Brathwaite keeps it out.
This time he offers no shot as the ball is way too outside off.
Fuller in length this time, the batter strokes it to mid off. He is a tad late on the shots he has played in this over.
This is fired on off, Campbell keeps it out. He has looked good until now.
FOUR! Nicely played! Waits for the ball to come to him and then guides it through the gap in the slip cordon. It goes down to the third man fence.
Campbell was late onto that one! On a length and around off, this one comes back in late. Campbell maybe first thought of leaving it but at the very end keeps it out.
Length delivery and outside off, Brathwaite is not interested in playing at those. Maiden by Anderson.
A good surprise bumper, Brathwaite though was upto the task as he ducks under it.
Another one outside off, the batter need not play at those.
A stifled appeal but nothing from the umpire. On middle and leg, Brathwaite looks to keep it out but misses. The ball hits him high on the pads.
On the stumps this time, KB gets right behind the line and defends it onto the ground. Good going by the two Windies openers till now.
Length and a little too wide outside off, it is left alone.
A good leave! Ben Stokes gets this one to come back in from outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it. The ball though does not come in enough to hit the off stump. Good delivery though.
On the fuller side, the batter mistimes his shot to mid off.
Bowls the sucker ball full and wide outside off, Campbell resists the temptation and lets it be.
Corrects his length and line by bowling it on off and just behind a driving length. JC keeps it out.

FOUR! If you cut, you should cut hard and that is exactly what Campbell did. It was there to be hit, short and outside off, he slashes at it with everything. The ball goes over the leaping point fielder and into the fence.
Starts off with a ball on the pads, John works it to mid-wicket.
Ben Stokes is on now.
Now bowls the one that goes straight on. Brathwaite picks the variation and works it to mid-wicket.

BEAUTY! Just too good that one. Unplayable to be honest. That started on middle and then started swinging away. Brathwaite plays inside the line, the ball whizzes past the outside edge and then goes agonizingly close past the off pole.
Bouncer and it has been ducked under.
Outside off and it has been left alone.
Good length and on off, JC pushes it towards cover for a quick run.
Loose stroke that one! Full and wide outside off, Campbell throws his bat at it away from his body but gets beaten. First real poor shot from him, not needed those.
Low bounce on this occasion but the ball is well outside off and Brathwaite lets it go. This is a maiden over but the Windies have been solid in the first 10.
A good length ball on off stump and slightly coming in, defended on the off side by Kraigg.
A late leave to this one outside the off stump.
Sprays this on leg stump line, KB misses his flick and gets hit on the thigh pad. Runs fine on the leg side but no run available.
A short one once more just outside off, good bounce but not enough pace to trouble Brathwaite. Rides the bounce and defends easily.
Wide outside off on a length, left alone by the right-hander.
Late inswing on this one after landing on off, JC adjusts and plays it towards mid on.
Another one on length and on off stump, John pushes this back towards the bowler.
This one lands on leg stump and comes straight on, Campbell presents a straight bat in defense.
Fuller length ball on middle and leg, flicked away to fine leg for a single.
Kept out from within the crease once more.
Short of a length ball on middle, defended off the back foot by KB.

Almost snuck through, an inside edge saves the batsman at the last moment. This was on a length and coming in with the angle, Campbell almost played it down the wrong line but the willow comes to his rescue.
Shortens the length once more outside off, defended back towards the bowler on the back foot.
Worked away off the pads by Campbell, wide of fine leg for a couple of runs.
Short of a length and above off stump, defended from within the crease.
Outside off and defended watchfully towards cover.
Curran has not got his line right so far. Length ball on the leg stump line, Campbell fails to get bat on ball and gets hit on the thigh pad.
This one comes in but is defended easily by Kraigg.
Shouldered arms to a ball outside off once more.
Lots of swing this time but way outside off and left alone by the batsman.
Length ball and it straightens after landing. Brathwaite misses his flick and gets hit high on the thigh pad.
Shortens the length this time, KB defends with a straight bat.
Full length ball just outside off, Kraigg comes ahead and pats it back to the bowler.
A little away movement again but the line is outside off, Brathwaite shoulders arms to it.
This time he gets right behind the line and defends it onto the ground.
The inside edge saves him there! Good length around middle, it shapes away a little. John tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
FOUR! Too short and it has been dispatched! Campbell picked the length early there and then pulls it over mid-wicket. It races to the fence. JC dealing in boundaries here.
Perfect! Fuller in length and around off, it comes back in. Kraigg with the swing works it towards fine leg and gets to the other end.
Shortish and around middle, KB keeps it out off the back foot. The ball is swinging a little, Curran needs to get it full, make use of the new ball.

Peach! An absolute peach from Anderson to end the over. The previous one came in and this one is on a length outside off and holds its line. Campbell tried to put bat on ball but plays for the swing and down the wrong line. The cherry whizzes past his outside edge. Brilliant last two balls from Jimmy. This would have surely put doubts in the debutant's mind.

How was that? An appeal from the English is turned down by Rod Tucker.  Looked like it was doing a little too much to the naked eye. A full and inswinging ball on middle. Campbell misses his flick and gets rapped on the pad, a loud appeal ensues but no reaction from the umpire. The replays show that the ball would have missed leg stump.
Length ball on the hips, kept out towards the mid-wicket region.
Once more outside off and once more, JC doesn't go fishing.
Well left outside off this time by the lefty.
Pretty full on middle and leg, easily worked away through square leg for a run.
Defended calmly this time. Good start so far for the Windies this.

FOUR! Lovely looking shot from Campbell. Doesn't seem to be over-awed by the situation. A short of a length ball outside off this time, John is quick to climb and cut it away stylishly through point for a boundary. Windies flair in that shot.
Quick single! Appreciated by those in the crowd. A length ball outside off, pushed towards cover-point by Brathwaite and his partner is quick to respond for a single.
Left alone outside off this time.
Curran trying to get this ball come in and bowls this on a fuller length outside off. KB defends on the front foot towards gully.
Fuller length ball on middle, Campbell unlike his partner is playing his shots. Flicks this away to fine leg for a single. Good positive intent.
Left alone outside off to end the over.
Goes back in his crease and defends this ball towards the off side.
Left alone outside off very late, the Brathwaite style.
Good ball on a length outside off, Kraigg lets the ball come on to his bat and defends it towards gully from right under his nose.
On the pads to the left-hander as well, worked away to fine leg for a single by JC. Windies reach double figures.
Very full one on leg stump from Jimmy, Brathwaite works it square on the leg side for a single.
FOUR! The second of the over. And through the same region. Bowled a tad outside off, Campbell comes ahead and angles this in the gap between gully and point. Runs away to the fence.
Fuller and on the pads, Campbell comes slightly ahead as he pushes this towards mid on.
Gets the right line and length this time, pushed back to the bowler.
Too close for comfort! This one is just above off stump and Campbell leaves it alone. Bounces above the pole luckily for the batsman.
Overcompensates too hard, bowls this way down leg.
FOUR! What a way to start off in Test cricket. A length ball outside off, Campbell just eases this one wide of gully and the ball races to the third man boundary. Windies and John off the mark!
Sam Curran to bowl from the other end.
Maiden to start off, the last one is left alone outside off.
Gets the perfect length this time and on top of off, KB defends not too comfortably but no scares.
Pushes this a little further up outside off, Kraigg lets it go.
Watchfully kept out once more.
Better line just outside off, defended easily.
Good swing first up, but the line was not that great. Starts off on leg stump, Brathwaite defends from the crease awkwardly.
A false start...

The players and the umpires have taken their positions post the national anthems. Kraigg Brathwaite and debutant, John Campbell to open for Windies while James Anderson has the new cherry in hand for the visitors. All set to go. Let's play...
TOSS -  The Windies won the toss and elected to bat.

Hello and welcome to 1st Test of the three-match series between the Windies and England. The visitors come into this game in very good form in this format, whereas, the hosts are not in the best of touches. They though will want to turn it around starting from this Test, however, it won't be easy against an English side which has started to come into its own under Root's captaincy. They are favourites heading into this game but the Windies can't be ruled out especially in their own backyard.
